reply:
TCP is a byte stream—no message boundaries. One `send()` doesn't guarantee one `recv()`, and vice versa. Multiple sends can arrive in one read, one send can split across multiple reads.

Your server is probably fine. The client must implement framing: a length prefix (first N bytes = message length), or a delimiter (newline, null byte, sentinel), then parse that buffer. Without it, you can't tell where one message ends and another begins on the receive side.

grade.note: Reply agrees TCP has no message boundaries and explains framing requirement, matching developer and ground truth.
